<abstract>Background: Hypertension (HTN) is a major cardiovascular risk factor and a leading cause of premature death, affecting ~30% of the global population. We used MR to distinguish causal from pleiotropic associations. Finally, we used clinical features and plasma protein expression data from ~50,000 UKBB participants to prioritize causal proteins significantly associated with incident HTN and related diseases using Cox models adjusted for age, sex, and body mass index (BMI). Results: From the 4,717 plasma proteins tested, we identified a CPP of 7 proteins associated with BP through 12 variants. The PS-PheWAS showed that the two strongest associations were for essential HTN ( p = 3.78×10 -36 ) and chronic kidney disease (CKD; p = 6.23×10 -9 ). MR supported causal effects of the expression of 5 of the 7 proteins for CKD and lifespan (CLMP, NCAN, PLXNB2, TCEA2, and WARS). Prospective analyses showed that plasma levels of one of them, WARS, were significantly and positively associated with the incidence of HTN, CKD, and mortality, independently of BMI ( Figure 1 ). Conclusion: Our strategy prioritized WARS as a genetically supported causal plasma protein positively associated with HTN, CKD, and mortality, highlighting its potential as a new therapeutic target for HTN.</abstract>

  secondary analysis of completed experiments, and original conference
  abstracts can qualify.
- `nonempirical`: review, systematic review, meeting report, editorial,
  commentary, perspective, correction, protocol, future proposal, method-only
  description, atlas/database/cohort resource, or other report without
  substantive current biological analysis and new results.
- `unclear`: the supplied text cannot distinguish these types.

Current methods and results override a generic metadata label. Future language
without completed analysis is nonempirical. If report type is not
`empirical_primary`, set all three downstream values to `not_assessed`.

Original-analysis override: a title containing `review`, `systematic review`,
or a misspelled variant does not force `nonempirical` when the abstract says
the current authors performed a new public-data/bioinformatics analysis and
reports its own substantive or numerical Results. Return
`empirical_primary` for that current original analysis. A literature search,
study selection, evidence synthesis, or summary of included studies remains
`nonempirical`.

Completion predicate rule: return `empirical_primary` even for a truncated
record when the current-report title states that an analysis
`reveals/identifies/finds` a result, or the fragment states `we
performed/analyzed/analysed/profiled` and names the analysis or result. Do not
use `unclear` merely because surrounding sentences are omitted. This rule does
not override an explicit review, protocol, commentary, or resource-only
description.

Step 2: `bio_health_scope`

- `yes`: humans, animals, cells, tissues, microorganisms, molecular biology,
  disease, health, lifespan, or another biological system.
- `no`: purely synthetic, mathematical, engineering, or non-biological work.
- `unclear`: application domain is not stated.

If biological scope is not `yes`, set aging and multi-omics to
`not_assessed`.

Step 3: `aging_process_relevance`

This is candidate retention, not final mechanistic grading. Use `yes` when the
current report analyzes any construct that the authors explicitly frame as
aging, ageing, biological age, or an aging-related biological process. The
construct may be an exposure, outcome, measured phenotype, group contrast,
mechanism, trajectory, mediator, marker, model, or intervention target.

FIRST LITERAL CHECK: before interpreting disease context, scan current Methods,
Results, or current-result assertions for the exact organismal outcome word
`lifespan`. If the report tests, associates, links, changes, decreases, or
increases any exposure, molecular feature, intervention, or condition against
`lifespan`, return `yes` and do not apply a disease-prognosis exclusion. Do not
silently replace the literal word `lifespan` with the broader category
`survival`. This title-stage rule intentionally retains the record for
full-text verification.

Use `yes` for any of these current-report patterns:

- biological or epigenetic age, age acceleration, aging clocks, aging
  trajectories, longevity, lifespan, healthspan, exceptional longevity,
  rejuvenation, geroprotection, or senolysis;
- an explicit current analysis that tests an exposure, gene, protein,
  molecular trait, intervention, or genetic instrument against `lifespan` as

integration.

- `yes`: the current report clearly analyzes at least two distinct broad

  metabolomics/lipidomics, microbiomics, or equivalent. GWAS/instruments plus

Future or ongoing multi-omics work does not count as current analysis. Two

Imaging, clinical variables, flow cytometry, demographics, and routine

<title>Abstract 4364377: An Integrative Strategy Combining Genetic, Proteomic, and Clinical Data Identifies Circulating WARS as a Candidate Target for Hypertension.</title>
<abstract>Background: Hypertension (HTN) is a major cardiovascular risk factor and a leading cause of premature death, affecting ~30% of the global population. Despite available treatments, ~20% of individuals live with drug-resistant HTN. Blood pressure (BP) regulation involves the endothelium in contact with circulating plasma proteins, which are easily pharmacologically accessible. Notably, drug targets with genetic support are 2.6 times more likely to succeed clinically. Using the tag variants from these loci, we calculated a polygenic score (PS) to perform a PS-based phenome-wide association study (PS-PheWAS) to assess the association of the CPP with HTN and its pleiotropy across 795 phenotypes measured in ~500,000 participants from the UK Biobank (UKBB). We used MR to distinguish causal from pleiotropic associations. Finally, we used clinical features and plasma protein expression data from ~50,000 UKBB participants to prioritize causal proteins significantly associated with incident HTN and related diseases using Cox models adjusted for age, sex, and body mass index (BMI). Results: From the 4,717 plasma proteins tested, we identified a CPP of 7 proteins associated with BP through 12 variants. The PS-PheWAS showed that the two strongest associations were for essential HTN ( p = 3.78×10 -36 ) and chronic kidney disease (CKD; p = 6.23×10 -9 ). MR supported causal effects of the expression of 5 of the 7 proteins for CKD and lifespan (CLMP, NCAN, PLXNB2, TCEA2, and WARS). Prospective analyses showed that plasma levels of one of them, WARS, were significantly and positively associated with the incidence of HTN, CKD, and mortality, independently of BMI ( Figure 1 ). Conclusion: Our strategy prioritized WARS as a genetically supported causal plasma protein positively associated with HTN, CKD, and mortality, highlighting its potential as a new therapeutic target for HTN.</abstract>

<abstract>Background Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a chronic progressive neurodegenerative disease impacting an estimated 44 million adults worldwide. The most highly significant differentially methylated loci also tracked with Mini Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores. Differentially methylated loci were enriched near brain and neurodegeneration-related genes (e.g., BDNF, BIN1, APOC1 ) validated using the genotype tissue expression project portal (GTex). Conclusions Our work shows that peripheral differential methylation between age-matched subjects with AD relative to healthy controls will provide opportunities to further investigate and validate differential methylation as a surrogate of disease.
